novel_mechanics_found: ft09 L4-L6 is a constraint-satisfaction / Lights-Out hybrid, fully decoded: (1) The board is an irregular grid of 6x6-px cells (pitch 8). PREDICATE cells display a 3x3 ring pattern: ring position BLACK(0) = that neighbor must MATCH the predicate's center color; ring '2' = must DIFFER; ring '3' = that neighbor is out-of-board or a predicate (no constraint). Predicates constrain their 8 surrounding cells. (2) A color legend in the top-right corner lists the level's cycle colors (L4: 9->8->12; L5/L6: two colors). Clicking a plain cell cycles its color one step. (3) L5 introduced 6-diamond-marked cells: clicking one flips ITSELF + the neighbors indicated by the positions of the 6-marks drawn inside the cell - a centered cross mark flips all 4 orthogonal neighbors (Lights-Out style). Predicates never flip. (4) L6 (finale): EVERY cell is marked, but the mark sits at the cell's TOP-CENTER = each press flips self + NORTH neighbor only. The mark's position inside the cell is a literal diagram of the flip mask - read it, don't assume the L5 cross. Solved as a GF(2) linear system (Gaussian elimination over 22 cells). (5) Coordinates are 1:1 display=grid on L4-L6 (unlike L3's halving camera). (6) Bottom row = 64-click move counter per level; plenty for direct solutions.
narrative: Replayed the 25-label banked prefix to L3, then decoded the predicate constraint language from pixel patterns alone: hypothesis (black=match, 2=differ) was confirmed by cross-predicate consistency (three predicates jointly forced one cell to the third color, exactly matching the legend). L4 fell first-try in 16 clicks. L5 added cross-flip Lights-Out cells; a probe click revealed the 5-cell flip, and the level fell in 21 clicks. L6 made every cell a flipper - the first 11-press batch assumed the L5 cross mask and produced 9 mismatches, whose exact pattern proved the true mask was self+north (the 6-mark's position inside the cell diagrams the mask); a GF(2) re-solve from the live state finished the game (GameState.WIN, 6/6). Self-ran the reproduction gate: the 83-label sequence reproduces the full clear (reached_level=6, reproduced=True).
gotchas: Predicate ring symbols: 0=neighbor must match center color, 2=must differ, 3=no constraint (out-of-board or predicate neighbor).
The 6-mark position inside a flipper cell diagrams its flip mask: centered cross marks = flips 4 orthogonal neighbors; top-center mark = flips north neighbor only. READ the mark, don't assume.
Flips onto predicate cells or off-board simply vanish (predicates never change).
Click coordinates are 1:1 with grid pixels on L4-L6; only L3 used a 2x display camera.
Color cycle per level is shown by the top-right legend column, in order (L4: 9->8->12->9).
Multi-flipper levels are GF(2) linear systems - solve with Gaussian elimination, don't greedy-click.
A wrong flip-model batch is recoverable: the mismatch pattern between predicted and actual state uniquely identifies the true mask, and a re-solve from the live state costs no reset.
Bottom-row counter = 64 clicks per level, refreshed on level-up; direct solutions use ~16-32.
